findings.body:
Setting `InsecureSkipVerify: true` on every `NewClient()` call disables TLS verification for all environments. If any production path reaches this client, a MITM attacker can impersonate the ledger.

```suggestion
	TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: false},
```

(Or gate the insecure transport behind a build tag / env var that is never enabled for prod builds.)

summary: The change unconditionally disables TLS certificate verification for every caller of `NewClient()`. The comment claims the bypass is staging-only, but nothing in the code enforces that scope, so the insecure client will also be used against production endpoints.

verification.reason: The head client factory unconditionally sets tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true} for every NewClient(), and the patch newly introduced that insecure transport (base used a plain http.Client). No env/build gate exists, so any caller would skip TLS verification.
